issues.description: The template file src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java does not provide the expected Farm class and animals List as specified in the problem statement UML and textual instructions. Instead the template defines a class named AnimalFarm and contains malformed/duplicated package and class content (including an inner 'package' declaration and duplicate class blocks). This structural mismatch (wrong class name, missing Farm class and missing animals List/ArrayList initialization) prevents students from implementing the required Farm type and following the UML/design described in the assignment. The solution repository implements a class named Farm with a List<Animal> animals and the expected methods, so the template is inconsistent with both the problem statement and the solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Replace the template src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java with a correct skeleton declaring public class Farm in package de.tum.cit.ase. The skeleton should include a private List<Animal> animals field, a no-argument constructor that initializes animals = new ArrayList<>(), and stubs/getters/setters for addAnimal, feedAllAnimals, singFarmSong, and singFarmSongVerse so students can implement the required behavior. Remove the incorrectly named AnimalFarm class and any duplicated package declarations or malformed code blocks.

issues.description: The template defines the Farm class file (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java) but declares the class as AnimalFarm, while the problem statement and solution expect a class named Farm. This mismatch between the file name and the declared class name (AnimalFarm vs Farm) breaks the conceptual mapping for students: the exercise describes and tests a Farm class, but the template provides a differently named class, causing compilation errors and confusion about which class to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the class declaration in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java from AnimalFarm to Farm (and fix any malformed/duplicate content within the file) so the template provides the expected Farm class that matches the problem statement and the solution. Ensure the class name and file name align and that methods and signatures (e.g., singFarmSong()) are declared on the Farm class.
